**Stonebeck: a quiet tape, an unreconciled gap**

Rating: underweight

The wire was quiet this session, and the prints came in line — precisely the conditions under which our prior counsels the most attention, not the least. A structurally cautious reading holds that calm surfaces are where fragilities accumulate unpriced, and the data here does not contradict that view so much as it declines to resolve it.

Consider the composition of return. The one-year return of +11.0% sits atop a year-to-date figure of only +1.1%, which is consistent with either a stalling trend or simply front-loaded gains now facing a harder second half — the data cannot distinguish these, and we decline to guess in its favor. Meanwhile the policy rate at 5.00% against cpi_now of 2.9% implies a real rate still meaningfully restrictive; a common counterargument that policy support resolves the stress presumes an easing path that the rate level itself does not yet confirm. The high-yield spread at 400bps is not alarming in isolation, but paired with a drawdown of +0.0% — that is, no drawdown at all despite the restrictive backdrop — it reads less like resilience and more like marks that have not yet been asked to move.

The reported_vs_public_gap of -0.2% is small, but its sign matters more than its size: marks running behind the public tape is the textbook shape of lag, however modest today. Picture the chart as a flat line for reported values riding just above a slightly higher public series — a small gap, but one that has not yet closed the other way.

Risk to this view: should the gap simply reflect noise rather than lag, and the quiet session persist into genuinely benign data, our caution may prove premature. We would watch the spread and the gap jointly before revising, and treat any easing of either as a prudent trigger to reassess rather than a signal to act on immediately.
